podcast.body: Recorded in 1945, this song features Sister Rosetta Tharpe playing a resonator guitar with noticeable ferocity. It was released before rock and roll was officially invented, leading some to consider it one of the very first rock and roll songs. "In 1945, she recorded a song called Strange Things Happening Every Day."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Recorded in September 1944, marking a significant collaboration with Sam Price on piano. This song is frequently credited as being one of the first rock and roll records and ushered in a new style for Tharp. "but nonetheless strange things happening every day, marks out the start of yet another new style for Tharp, and its yet another song, often credited as the first rock and roll record."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
